Subject: Re: About the implementation of a Point-quarter method and a
random walk procedure for establishing the sampling points.


Fernando, I would not use that approach at all. It is a very inefficient
way to estimate absolute density. Random walk does not give you a
representative sample to estimate density. You need to define the area
for which you require density estimates, then take a random/representative
sample of points or lines within that area. Lines (line or strip transect
sampling) is likely to be far more efficient than points.

I suggest you read one of our books on this subject before implementing a
design. The disadvantages of your proposed approach are spelt out on p294
of our 1993 book, which is available free on our web pages. The 2001 book
would be better (see our web pages for how to get it), as it addresses
survey design issues in much greater detail than the 1993 book (chapter
7). Point-to-nearest-object methods are summarized in pp223-5 of that
book.

Steve Buckland
